passage:
Subject: Thank you, and an update

Dear Shalini didi,

Thank you for Sunday's mock interview. I'll admit it stung when you said my answers rambled and that I kept looking at the table instead of at you. I went home a little red in the face, embarrassed at how much I needed to hear. But you were right. Since then I have cut my "tell me about yourself" to under a minute, practised with my phone recording, and written three project stories in a few lines each. The real interview is on Thursday and I will write to tell you how it goes. Thank you for giving up your evening for me 🙏

Lalremsiami

qa.a: The real interview is on Thursday.

qa.q: How does Lalremsiami feel about the feedback?
qa.a: Lalremsiami feels thankful but a little embarrassed, since it stung and left the face red but was needed.

qa.q: What does Lalremsiami plan to do after the interview?
qa.a: Lalremsiami will write to Shalini to tell how it goes, so the help is reported back on.

qa.q: How might Shalini feel on getting this email?
qa.a: Shalini may be pleased that the honest feedback was used and appreciated, and glad to hear how the interview goes.

grounding: A senior gave a mock interview and honest feedback; Lalremsiami thanks Shalini, applies it and promises to report back.

passage:
'Pranav-bhaiya, got a minute?'
'Kishore! How did the interview go?'
'That's why I'm here. First, thank you. Properly. That mock interview on Saturday was brutal.'
'Too brutal?'
'No. When you said my answers sounded like I'd memorised a website, I wanted to disappear.'
'Sorry about that.'
'Don't be. I went home and rewrote all of them with my own examples. The canteen inventory thing, the robotics club budget. And today when they asked about teamwork, I told the robotics story.'
'And?'
'They asked me three follow-ups on it. They were actually interested.'
'That's great, man.'
'Second round is Friday. Can I tell you how it goes?'
'You'd better. Most people take the mock and I never hear from them again.'
Kishore grinned, a bit red in the face. 'Not me, bhaiya.'

qa.q: What was Kishore feeling when Pranav said the answers sounded memorised?
qa.a: Kishore felt embarrassed and hurt, wanting to disappear, though Kishore is now grateful for it.
Kishore applied the feedback by rewriting answers with real examples, came back to report, and promised to share how Friday goes.

qa.q: How does Pranav see Kishore coming back?
qa.a: Pranav is pleased and a little surprised, since most people take the mock and never report back.

grounding: Shows gratitude to a senior whose honest mock-interview feedback stung, expressed by thanking him, using the feedback and reporting back.

passage: I'm Himani, and I still go a bit red remembering Ojas's feedback. He was two years senior, already working at a consulting firm, and he gave up his Sunday to do a mock interview with me over a video call. At the end he said, very kindly, 'You speak fast when you're nervous, and you never actually answered why you want this job.' I said thank you, closed the laptop and cried a little. For a week I didn't reply to his follow-up message, because I was embarrassed. Then I realised that vanishing after someone gives you their Sunday is rude. So I wrote to him: what I'd changed, that I'd practised slowing down with a timer, and that my real answer to 'why this job' was my father's small printing shop. I got the offer in March. Ojas was the second person I called.

qa.q: What did Ojas give up to do the mock interview?
What was Himani feeling in the week after the mock interview?
qa.a: Himani felt embarrassed and a little hurt, which is why the follow-up message went unanswered for a week.

qa.q: What did Himani do right in the end?
qa.a: Himani wrote to thank Ojas, explained what had changed, like practising slowing down with a timer, and later called with the news.

qa.q: How might Ojas have felt getting Himani's message after a week of silence?
qa.a: Ojas was likely glad and reassured that the feedback helped and that his Sunday had been worth it.

grounding: A first-person account of thankful embarrassment after a senior's honest mock interview, and choosing to report back rather than vanish.
